question: Can I release a non-native aquatic species into a lake frequented by fish in Canada?
generated_answer:
Releasing non-native aquatic species into Canadian waters is generally prohibited by law. The Fisheries Act and the Species at Risk Act protect native species and ecosystems from invasive species. Releasing non-native species can cause significant harm to native fish populations, disrupt ecosystems, and lead to costly control measures. It is essential to follow regulations and consult with local authorities before releasing any species into the environment. 

If you have a non-native species that you can no longer care for, consider contacting local pet stores, aquariums, or wildlife rehabilitation centers to find a responsible solution. 

For more information, you can refer to the following resources:
- Fisheries and Oceans Canada: [https://www.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/science/aquatic-ecosystems/biological-impacts/non-native-aquatic-species-eng.html](https://www.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/science/aquatic-ecosystems/biological-impacts/non-native-aquatic-species-eng.html)
- Environment and Climate Change Canada: [https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/ecosystems/invasive-species.html](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/ecosystems/invasive-species.html) 

Remember, releasing non-native species into the wild can have serious consequences and is generally not allowed. Always seek advice from local authorities or experts before taking any action. 

If you have any further questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to ask.
